_meta.question: How much space do the raw document bodies take, and should they be compressed?
_meta.answer_in_one_line: Compression is the wrong first move. 169 MB of the 302 MB file is unreclaimed housekeeping debt that costs 2 seconds and zero risk to remove — four times what compressing every body would save.

where_the_space_is.archive_family_share: 56.3 MB of 57.8 MB (97.5%) is session-archive / transcript / session

safety.search_parity: doc FTS and memory search return identical top-5 hashes on every probe query

the_cheap_win_fts5_optimize_plus_vacuum.why_it_had_grown: FTS5 writes each transaction as a new segment and only merges them on demand. Neither VACUUM nor INSERT INTO <fts>(<fts>) VALUES('optimize') appears anywhere in src/ or hooks/, so segments have accumulated since February and freed pages were never returned to the OS.
the_cheap_win_fts5_optimize_plus_vacuum.volatility_note: document_fts_data measured 90.6, 52.8 and 73.9 MB within a few minutes of each other as background writes triggered partial merges. Any single reading of it is a snapshot, not a level.

does_sqlite_have_built_in_compression.short_answer: No. Stock SQLite has no transparent page or column compression.

options.ZIPVFS: Transparent page-level compression, but it ships only with the commercial SQLite Encryption Extension. Paid licence.
options.sqlite-zstd: Third-party Rust extension, transparent row-level compression. Would have to be loaded by every process that opens the DB — CLI, MCP server, daemon and each hook subprocess. Operational cost is the real price, not the ratio.
options.sqlar: An archive FORMAT that stores compressed files in a table. Not transparent compression of an existing schema.
options.application_level: Compress documents.body yourself before INSERT. No extension needed, works everywhere.

if_bodies_were_compressed_anyway.note: Each body compressed alone, which is how a column would work — no cross-document dictionary. Transcripts are repetitive English so ~3.7x with plain zlib is expected.
if_bodies_were_compressed_anyway.residual_gain: Applied AFTER optimize+vacuum, this takes 133.4 MB to roughly 91 MB — still 31%, but no longer the dominant term.
if_bodies_were_compressed_anyway.the_catch: document_fts is external-content (content='documents', content_rowid='id'), so FTS5 reads documents.body directly. Compressing that column to a BLOB breaks the FTS rebuild path (core.py:1173 populates the index by selecting body out of documents) and any code reading body without decompressing. FTS5 keeps no copy of its own — that is why document_fts has no _content shadow table — so the index cannot be rebuilt from itself.

recommended_order: 1. FTS5 optimize on both indexes, then VACUUM. 169 MB, ~2s, no schema change, search output byte-identical.
2. Run the held archive prune (208 docs, 13 MB of body) and purge the 838 expired soft-deletes, then VACUUM again.
3. Only then consider compression, and only with a decompress shim on every body read plus a rebuild path that does not select raw body.
4. Add optimize+VACUUM to the daily cleanup so this debt stops accruing. That is the actual fix; step 1 is a one-off.
